candidates.name: sieger1010/h2a
candidates.what_it_holds: Standardized U.S. Department of Labor H-2A agricultural seasonal-worker employment disclosure data, FY2008 through FY2025 Q3 (17+ years). Processed exports in processed_exports/ as CSV, Pickle, Feather, Parquet, and a SQLite DB. Fields include employer name (with known aliasing issues, e.g. North Carolina Growers Association), wage data, work-site location, employment start/end dates, worker certification counts, and DOL case numbers (some duplicated). README notes reported fields change across years so YoY comparisons need care; Python cleaning scripts are in-repo.
candidates.why_useful: H-2A is a seasonal-migrant-worker visa program tied to harvest calendars in specific U.S. counties/states; a point-in-time, multi-year, county-level labor inflow series is a proxy for seasonal rural/agricultural-region short-term-rental and worker-housing demand (relevant to niche STR demand pockets and to broader seasonal-labor-market strength as a consumer-spending input) rather than a direct ABNB KPI driver, but it is a genuinely large, long, well-processed public dataset with no equivalent already held.
candidates.size_hint: 17+ years of DOL H-2A disclosure records; multi-format exports (CSV/Parquet/SQLite)
candidates.last_activity: unspecified (repo found via gh search, not dated in this pass)

candidates.name: JMStratil/Create_DateDataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Base-R script that builds a daily calendar panel with school holidays, public holidays, and derived 'exposure' variables, computed from a Gregorian Easter algorithm and statutory holiday rules (no temperature/shapefile/population data, per its own description). Country/region scope and date range were not resolved on WebFetch (repo showed as empty on a second look, updated 8 Sep 2026, 0 stars) so contents could not be independently confirmed beyond the gh search snippet.
candidates.why_useful: If it actually runs, a generated school/public-holiday panel is a low-cost way to build an academic-calendar / long-weekend feature for nowcasting nights (gap area: student and school-break travel timing), but confirmation failed (WebFetch reported an empty repo) so this is speculative and should be re-checked before use.
candidates.geography: unclear, likely a single country (statutory-rule based)

candidates.name: cdmerchant13/anchorpoint
candidates.what_it_holds: A prototype community/social app for U.S. military spouses coping with Permanent Change of Station (PCS) moves. No dataset of PCS move volumes, dates, or bases is committed; it is an application, not a data source.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms the military-moves search surface is thin on GitHub in the app form we found; flagged only to record that it exists and was checked and rejected (no data).

candidates.name: PADM-23/APAYO
candidates.what_it_holds: Hackathon (Junction Asia 2026) iOS medical-intake app for migrant seasonal farm workers in Gyeongsangbuk-do, South Korea. Bundles ~3,415 clinic and 1,141 pharmacy locations from Korea's Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service open data, used only for facility lookup inside the app — no worker counts, arrival dates, or travel-demand data.
candidates.why_useful: Checked because it combines 'medical' and 'seasonal migrant worker' in scope; contains no time series or volume data relevant to travel demand, only a static facility list for a single Korean province. Included for completeness/negative result.
candidates.size_hint: small app repo, 0 stars, MIT license

notes: This theme surfaced very little on GitHub via gh search repos: 'academic calendar dataset' and 'medical tourism dataset' returned zero results outright, and the seasonal-worker/military/student-visa searches mostly returned unrelated apps or hit the 30/min shared rate limit (two of six searches got HTTP 403, both retried once successfully after a 45s wait per instructions). A generic OR query ('SEVIS OR study abroad OR spring break dates data') was too broad and returned the top global GitHub repos by stars (pandas, redis, etc.) with no relevant hits, confirming this niche is not well represented by committed datasets on GitHub under these keywords. WebSearch (site:github.com ...) was unavailable for this run — the session had already exhausted its 200-query web-search budget before I could use it, so I could not cross-check via search engine the way the modality brief suggests as a fallback; only WebFetch on already-known URLs was usable. Best real find is sieger1010/h2a (DOL H-2A seasonal agricultural-worker disclosure data, FY2008-2025Q3, multi-format), which is adjacent to the theme (labor migration/seasonal demand) but not a direct STR/travel dataset — worth another agent's look for equivalent H-2B (non-agricultural seasonal, more hospitality/tourism-adjacent) or J-1 (student/exchange visitor) repackaged datasets, and for Zenodo/Dataverse hosts (not searchable via gh) covering university academic calendars (e.g. a scraped registrar-calendar corpus) or medical-tourism flow data, which likely live off GitHub entirely. A follow-up scout with fresh WebSearch budget should retry: 'registrar academic calendar API github', 'J-1 exchange visitor SEVIS data github', 'NCES IPEDS enrollment calendar github', and 'medical tourism flow Mexico dental dataset github'.
